$comment: LED2, the fourth telltale escape via -- the one u47b deliberately left out.
/U12_RSTN STAIRCASES AROUND this via. It arrives from the west at y=87.960,
zigzags through (235.24..235.28, 88.24..88.76) to get past the via, and
leaves west again at y=89.040. That detour exists because of the via, and it
is what makes every obvious escape illegal:
north  y<=87.450 (clear of the pad)  0.083 to the y=87.960 run    NO
south  y>=89.350                     negative to the y=89.040 run  NO
east   x>=236.5 clears by 0.793, but the Bottom track reaching it must
cross the staircase: -0.034 at x=235.5                      NO
West works. The via lands at (233.000,88.500) -- outside the pad, its 0.6 mm
copper clearing the pad edge by 0.150 mm -- and the Bottom track it already
sits on simply gets shorter. Clearance to /U12_RSTN is 0.113 against the
0.113 is tight and is recorded as such. It is accepted because what it
replaces is worse and certain: a via centred in the pad wicks solder down the
barrel at reflow (~22% of the deposit on the estimate on record), giving an
asymmetric fillet and a tilted LED behind a lens. A legal 0.113 mm gap beats
a guaranteed assembly defect, and this same net is already documented running
at 0.1030 elsewhere on the board.
The alternative -- re-routing /U12_RSTN so the staircase is unnecessary --
would open real margin here and is the better long-term fix. It is a separate
change to a working net and is not attempted in this spec.

steps.step: 1/1  LED2 -- slide the via west, out of the pad, along its own Bottom run
